source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 71:1-24 . The Psalmist, probably in old age, appeals to God for help from his enemies, pleading his past favors, and stating his present need; and, in confidence of a hearing, he promises his grateful thanks and praise.

entries.heading: 3. given commandment
entries.text: 3. given commandment --literally, "ordained," as in Ps 44:4; 68:28 . rock . . . fortress -- ( Ps 18:2 ).

6-9. His history from early infancy illustrated God's care, and his wonderful deliverances were at once occasions of praise and ground of confidence for the future. my praise . . . of thee --literally, "in" or "by Thee" ( Ps 22:25 ).
10, 11. The craft and malicious taunts of his enemies now led him to call for aid (compare the terms used, 2Sa 17:12; Ps 3:2; 7:2 ).
14-16. The ruin of his enemies, as illustrating God's faithfulness, is his deliverance, and a reason for future confidence.

entries.heading: 15. for I know . . . thereof
entries.text: 15. for I know . . . thereof --innumerable, as he had not time to count them.

entries.heading: 16. in the strength
entries.text: 16. in the strength --or, relying on it. thy righteousness --or, faithful performance of promises to the pious ( Ps 7:17; 31:1 ).
17-21. Past experience again encourages. taught me, &c.--by providential dealings.

entries.heading: 20. depths of the earth
entries.text: 20. depths of the earth --debased, low condition.

entries.heading: 21. increase,
entries.text: 21. increase, &c.--that is, the great things done for me ( Ps 71:19 ; compare Ps 40:5 ).
22-24. To the occasion of praise he now adds the promise to render it. will . . . praise --literally, "will thank." even thy truth --as to Thy truth or faithfulness.
